records.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go the import of github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck was removed, and the code now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() ("db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()"), but the diff shows no added import for the new internal package (e.g. github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql). Without importing that package (and likely aliasing it to avoid clashing with the stdlib database/sql name), this will not compile.

records.issue_text: TablesList in parser.go always fails because duckDB.RunCommands is a stub, breaking table name extraction and reference resolution for {{refId}} references
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now does `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()` and then calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`. The newly added pkg/expr/sql/db.go defines `RunCommands` as a stub that always returns `"not implemented"` (and returns empty string), so TablesList cannot succeed and will always error at runtime. This breaks table-name extraction (and any downstream logic depending on it).
records.stripped_text: TablesList in parser.go always fails because duckDB.RunCommands is a stub, breaking table name extraction and reference resolution for {{refId}} references

records.issue_text: enableSqlExpressions always returns false due to contradictory dead logic, making the FlagSqlExpressions feature flag non-functional and causing all QueryTypeSQL requests to fail unconditionally
records.rationale:
In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() is implemented with contradictory/dead logic and returns false on all paths:

```go
enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
if enabled { return false }
return false
```

Then in ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL it unconditionally rejects SQL queries when !enabled:

```go
enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)
if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }
```

So FlagSqlExpressions can never enable SQL expressions and all QueryTypeSQL requests fail with that error.
records.stripped_text: enableSqlExpressions always returns false due to contradictory dead logic, making the FlagSqlExpressions feature flag non-functional and causing all QueryTypeSQL requests to fail unconditionally

records.issue_text: SQL injection-prone escaping pattern: strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1) interpolated into fmt.Sprintf SQL instead of parameter binding, persisting in the new stub DB interface
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList still does `rawSQL = strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)` and then interpolates it into a SQL string via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` before calling `duckDB.RunCommands(...)` (now `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()`). Even though the new in-memory DB is currently a stub (`RunCommands` returns `errors.New("not implemented")`), the diff shows the continued reliance on manual escaping + string interpolation rather than parameter binding, which is a substantive security/design concern to address when the DB implementation is filled in.

records.issue_text: Per-call NewInMemoryDB() allocation in RunCommands means no connection/engine reuse, a resource concern once the stubs are implemented
records.rationale: The diff shows new call sites that instantiate a fresh in-memory DB for each operation (e.g., `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` before calling `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`, and `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` before `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`). This pattern implies no reuse of any underlying engine/connection once `DB` is implemented, which is a plausible resource/perf concern. It’s not a current correctness defect because `DB` methods are stubs returning `not implemented`.

records.issue_text: TablesList retains DuckDB-specific json_serialize_sql SQL against the stub DB, leaking abstraction details into the caller
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList still builds a DuckDB-specific command (`cmd := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)`) but now uses `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()` (after removing `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`). The new `NewInMemoryDB()` in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns a stub DB whose `RunCommands` always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so TablesList will fail at runtime and the DuckDB-specific SQL is now incompatible with the stub abstraction.
